channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Embezzlement of 13.9 Billion Soums in Wastewater Treatment Plant Construction Identified
item.description: The Department for Combating Economic Crimes under the Prosecutor General's Office of Uzbekistan reported the embezzlement of 13.9 billion Uzbek soums in the construction of a wastewater treatment plant in Nurafshon city, Tashkent region. Officials allegedly submitted false data for construction work, leading to the misappropriation of budget funds. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Tajikistan and Regional Countries Agree on Water Resource Monitoring
item.description: At the 95th meeting of the Interstate Coordination Water Commission of Central Asia in Turkmenbashi, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan discussed water resource management. They reviewed the 2026 vegetation period water intake and reservoir operation, and agreed to develop an automated water accounting system for the Syr Darya basin.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission Adjusts Number of Deputy Seats in Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan's Central Election Commission has revised the number of deputy seats in several regional and city maslikhats (local representative bodies). Changes include reductions in Aktobe and some Almaty region districts, and increases in Taraz and newly established maslikhats. The methodology for calculating seats based on population has also been updated.

item.title: Astana to provide one-time financial aid to people with disabilities
item.description: Astana will provide one-time social assistance to residents ahead of International Day of Persons with Disabilities on October 11. The aid amounts vary based on disability group: I group receives 20 MCI, II group and children with disabilities receive 10 MCI, and III group receives 5 MCI. No application is needed as recipients are identified from government data.

item.title: Nobel Laureate's Startup Develops Device to Extract Water from Air
item.description: California-based startup Atoco, founded by Nobel laureate Omar Yaghi, has created a device using metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to extract water from air. The system can collect up to 300 liters daily, even in low humidity (13%), requiring only slight heating. The water quality is comparable to distilled water.

item.title: Kazakhstan Real Estate Market: Rising Prices, Falling Transactions, No Imminent Collapse
item.description: The decline in real estate transactions in Kazakhstan, despite rising prices, is attributed to increased construction costs, not a market bubble. Experts note that higher material and VAT costs are driving up prices for new builds. This trend is expected to continue impacting buyers in the coming years.

item.title: China Tightens Export Conditions for Electric Vehicles to Tajikistan
item.description: New regulations from China are impacting Chinese exporters, including those supplying electric vehicles to Tajikistan. The article details the new requirements, the volume of electric vehicles imported by Tajikistan from China, and market participants' reactions to these changes.

item.title: UN: Over 581,000 migrants returned from Iran to Afghanistan this year
item.description: The UN Refugee Agency reports that 581,600 Afghan citizens have returned from Iran to Afghanistan this year. Of these, 492,300 were expelled by Iran, constituting 85% of all returns. These large-scale returns place significant pressure on essential services, housing, and livelihoods in Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Foreign Currency Inflows Exceed Outflows for First Time in Three Years
item.description: Kazakhstan's current account balance showed a surplus of $2.4 billion in the first half of 2026, a significant improvement from a $3.6 billion deficit last year. This shift is attributed to export growth outpacing import growth, with goods exports increasing by 27.1%.

item.title: Billions in Violations: Road Work Suppliers in Kazakhstan Used Others' Documents for Qualification
item.description: Kazakhstan's Chief Transport Prosecutor's Office uncovered violations in road construction and repair procurement, where suppliers used unqualified personnel's documents. In one case, documents of a non-employee were used for a 2.4 billion tenge project. Legal action is being taken against non-compliant entities.

item.title: Ukrainian woman detained in Kazakhstan for Russia released and left for EU
item.description: A Ukrainian citizen, Lyubov Rozhanskaya, detained in Kazakhstan at Russia's request, has been released from pre-trial detention and has left for an EU country. Ukrainian authorities, including the Foreign Ministry and Ombudsman, advocated for her release. She was detained at Astana airport on October 1st.

item.title: Kazakhstan plans to introduce state control over developer activities
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to implement state control over the activities of construction developers. Currently, developers are not subject to state control and supervision, making it impossible to apply administrative sanctions. Amendments to the law are planned to clarify the competencies of condominium object management chairpersons.

item.title: Head of company processing oil waste without license sentenced in Aktobe
item.description: The head of the "ZHAN-AMI and K" LLP company was sentenced in Aktobe for illegally processing over 1,400 tons of hazardous oil waste without a license between 2024-2025. The company earned 393 million tenge from this activity. He received a 2.5-year restricted liberty sentence, with illegal income confiscated.

item.title: US, South Korean, and Chinese companies interested in privatizing UzAuto Motors
item.description: Companies from the US, South Korea, and China have expressed interest in acquiring UzAuto Motors and UzAuto Powertrain. The State Assets Management Agency stated that the privatization process began two years ago and involves an international consultant. The sale will be conducted through competitive international tenders.

item.title: Astana residents warned of military aviation flights and street closures for international events
item.description: Astana will implement traffic restrictions on certain streets from October 10-14 due to preparations for international political events. Military aviation training flights will also take place in the capital's airspace starting October 9. Authorities request understanding from residents and visitors regarding these security measures.

item.title: Astana to Close Roads and Conduct Military Aviation Exercises
item.description: Astana will implement temporary traffic restrictions on certain streets from October 10-14 due to upcoming international political events. Military aviation flight exercises are scheduled from October 9. The State Security Service requests understanding from residents and visitors regarding security measures for these significant events.

item.title: Military Aircraft Flying Over Astana Due to International Political Events
item.description: Military aviation training flights have been conducted over Astana since October 9, with temporary traffic restrictions on some city streets planned from October 10-14. The State Security Service announced that resources from special state bodies, law enforcement, and armed forces will be mobilized to ensure security for upcoming international political events.

item.title: Kazakh Company Director Sentenced for Illegal Processing of Oil Waste
item.description: A director of a Kazakh company has been sentenced for illegally processing over 1,400 tons of hazardous oil waste without a license. The company illegally earned 393 million tenge. The director received a sentence of 2 years and 6 months of freedom restriction, but was released from the main punishment due to an amnesty law. The illicitly obtained funds were confiscated for the state.

item.title: Kazakh Businessman Sentenced to 10 Years for $2.2 Million Fraud
item.description: A businessman in Uralsk has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for defrauding $2.2 million. The court found him guilty of large-scale fraud. He created a company, KSS, and devised a scheme to transfer funds to his US-based company by falsely claiming the need to purchase equipment. The court also considered a previous sentence.

item.title: Uzbek Deputy Interior Minister's Acquittal Questioned by Higher Official
item.description: An Uzbek deputy interior minister stated that the innocence of former Deputy Interior Minister Bekmurod Abdullayev and other convicted employees has been fully reviewed. He indicated that questions regarding the investigation and sentencing should be directed to the relevant authorities. The review reportedly covered Abdullayev and other officials, addressing their innocence.

item.title: Turkmen Political Prisoner Mansur Mingelov's Health Deteriorates
item.description: The health of Turkmen political prisoner Mansur Mingelov has worsened, with his bone tuberculosis reportedly flaring up. Mingelov, held in a prison hospital, suffers from tuberculosis arthritis affecting his knees, spine, and bone tissue. He requires crutches and assistance to move. His family's request for early release due to illness was denied.

item.title: North Aral Sea volume increases by 4.6 billion cubic meters
item.description: The water volume in the North Aral Sea has reached 23.5 billion cubic meters, up from 18.9 billion in 2022. Approximately 1.5 billion cubic meters of water have been released into the sea since early 2026. This achievement is attributed to water diplomacy and coordinated reservoir operations on the Syr Darya River.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee proposes Central Bank review loan payment mechanism
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has submitted a proposal to the Central Bank regarding loan payments. The committee objects to overpaid funds not being directed towards the principal loan amount and requests a review of the calculation mechanism to benefit consumers.

item.title: Kazakhstan citizens sent to war in Ukraine after arriving in Russia for work
item.description: A 20-year-old Kazakhstani man, seeking work in Russia, claims he was sent to fight in Ukraine after signing documents he didn't understand due to the language barrier. His mother is desperately trying to bring him home, recounting his initial desire to earn money for their unfinished house.

item.title: Kazatomprom Refuses Uranium Sale to Russian Company, Agrees to Supply China
item.description: Kazakhstan's national uranium company, Kazatomprom, did not approve the sale of natural uranium to Uranium One Group, linked to Russia's Rosatom. However, shareholders approved a deal to supply uranium concentrate to China's State Nuclear Uranium Resource Development Company Limited (SNURDC).

item.title: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy Inspects Dushanbe's CHP-2 Plant Readiness for Winter
item.description: Tajikistan's Deputy Minister of Energy and Water Resources, Sharif Mahmadzoda, visited Dushanbe's Heat and Power Plant (CHP-2) to assess its preparation for the winter period. The plant has an installed capacity of 400 MW of electricity and 235 Gcal of heat. Ensuring reliable operation is crucial for supplying the capital's residents and institutions.

item.title: Tajik Scholars Can Receive Financial Aid for Research in the United States
item.description: Tajik scholars can now apply for the Fulbright Program's scholarship for the 2027-2028 academic year. The U.S. Embassy in Tajikistan announced that applications are open until November 6. The program supports Tajik academics with doctoral degrees to conduct research at American universities, prioritizing those with over 10 years of experience. Fields like AI, digital technologies, and energy are favored.

item.title: US Senator Rubio Warns Russia-Ukraine War Could Escalate into Regional Conflict
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio warned that Russia's war in Ukraine is at an impasse but could escalate into a wider regional conflict if either side takes dangerous actions. Speaking in Lisbon, Rubio stated that Washington believes the conflict must ultimately be resolved through negotiations and is ready to support diplomatic efforts. He cautioned that escalation could involve sabotage in neighboring NATO countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Law on Persons with Disabilities Contradicts UN Convention, Experts Say
item.description: Uzbekistan's legislation allows for deprivation of legal capacity by court order, contradicting Article 12 of the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. International expert Yanina Arseneva highlighted this at a human rights forum in Tashkent. The article focuses on the independent decision-making rights of individuals with disabilities. Over 1.06 million people with disabilities reside in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Astana to Host International Political Events, Causing Road Closures and Military Aircraft Flights
item.description: Astana will implement road restrictions from October 10 to 14 due to several international political events. The measures involve special state, law enforcement, and armed forces resources. Military aviation training flights will also take place in the capital's airspace starting October 9. Residents and guests are asked for understanding regarding security measures.

item.title: Italian Opposition Accuses Meloni Government of Attempting to Retain Power Through Electoral Reform
item.description: Italy's parliament has approved a significant electoral law reform proposed by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's coalition. The opposition claims the reform, which introduces a proportional system and grants bonus seats to the winning coalition, is an attempt to secure an advantage for the incumbent government. They intend to challenge the reform in the Constitutional Court.

item.title: UN Committee Urges Kazakhstan Not to Extradite Yulia Emelianova to Russia
item.description: The UN Committee Against Torture has requested Kazakhstan to halt the extradition of Yulia Emelianova to Russia pending a complaint review. Emelianova, a former associate of Alexei Navalny, has been detained in Almaty since August. Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office approved Russia's extradition request in January.

item.title: Tokayev Attends CIS Heads of State Council Meeting in Avaza
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived at the "Avaza" complex to participate in the meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the CIS member states. The meeting is expected to cover various aspects of cooperation among the Commonwealth of Independent States.

item.title: Tashkent Mayor Discusses Capital's Infrastructure Challenges and Development Priorities
item.description: Tashkent Mayor Shavkat Umurzakov acknowledges that the city's infrastructure is struggling to keep pace with rapid population growth and development. In an interview, he addressed how officials plan to tackle issues like education, healthcare, land reclamation, and air pollution, emphasizing resident participation in urban decisions.

item.title: UK Imposes Sanctions on Three Kyrgyz Companies and One Director
item.description: The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions on three Kyrgyz companies – TokenSpot CJSC, Tsunami Payments LLC, and Processing KG OJSC – along with its director, Ulan Bukabaev. The UK Foreign Ministry stated these measures are part of the sanctions regime against Russia. The companies face asset freezes and restrictions, while Bukabaev is banned from entering the UK and holding directorships.

item.title: Kazatomprom Rejects Uranium Deal with Russian Firm, Approves Supply to China
item.description: Kazakhstan's national uranium company, Kazatomprom, did not approve a deal to supply natural uranium to Uranium One Group, linked to Russia's Rosatom. Shareholders abstained or voted against the deal. However, Kazatomprom approved a contract for uranium concentrate sales to China's State Nuclear Uranium Resource Development Company Limited.

item.title: Tajikistan and Turkmenistan Presidents Discuss Strengthening Bilateral Ties
item.description: The presidents of Tajikistan and Turkmenistan, Emomali Rahmon and Serdar Berdimuhamedov, met in Avaza to discuss enhancing bilateral relations. They expressed interest in further strengthening ties and cooperation across political, economic, transport, energy, and cultural spheres, aiming to deepen their strategic partnership.

item.title: Kyiv Mayor Advises Residents to Leave Capital if Possible Amidst Russian Attacks
item.description: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko advised residents to temporarily leave the capital if possible due to Russian attacks on critical infrastructure. He stated the city is entering a 'survival mode' and warned of a potential large-scale crisis. Energy supply disruptions occurred, and the sewage system temporarily stopped accepting wastewater. Klitschko emphasized that full evacuation is not planned, as it would benefit Russia.

item.title: Aircraft Catches Fire at Riyadh Airport Following Houthi Attack Claim
item.description: An aircraft caught fire at Riyadh Airport after a claimed Houthi attack. The Houthis asserted they launched a ballistic missile at the airport. Saudi officials have not confirmed the attack. The incident occurred, leading to the aircraft fire. Further details are awaited regarding the event.

item.title: Shrinking Caspian Sea's Growing Military Significance Discussed by Coastal States
item.description: Coastal states are meeting in Turkmenistan's Avaza tourist zone to discuss the shrinking Caspian Sea and its increasing military significance. The Caspian Ecological Summit addresses the sea's ecosystem and resource use, with notable water level drops impacting shipping. Kazakhstan's ports of Aktau and Kuryk require dredging, affecting the Trans-Caspian transport route. The sea's water level has fallen significantly, with projections indicating further decline.
